title: Introduction to Machine Learning
text: Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence that enables systems to learn from data and improve from experience without being explicitly programmed.

title: Deep Learning Fundamentals
text: Deep learning uses neural networks with many layers to model complex patterns in data. It powers image recognition, natural language processing, and speech synthesis.

title: Natural Language Processing Overview
text: NLP enables computers to understand, interpret, and generate human language. Applications include translation, sentiment analysis, and question answering.

title: Information Retrieval Systems
text: Information retrieval is the science of searching for information in documents. Modern search engines use inverted indexes, ranking algorithms, and relevance feedback.

title: BM25 Ranking Algorithm
text: BM25 is a bag-of-words retrieval function that ranks documents based on query term frequencies, inverse document frequency, and document length normalization.

title: Vector Space Models
text: Vector space models represent documents and queries as vectors in a high-dimensional space. Cosine similarity measures the angle between vectors to compute relevance.

title: Transformer Architecture
text: Transformers use self-attention mechanisms to process sequences. BERT and GPT are transformer models pre-trained on large corpora and fine-tuned for downstream tasks.

title: Sentence Embeddings
text: Sentence embeddings encode the semantic meaning of text into dense vectors. Models like sentence-transformers produce embeddings useful for semantic similarity tasks.

title: FAISS for Approximate Nearest Neighbours
text: FAISS is a library for efficient similarity search in large vector databases. IVF indexes partition vectors into clusters for fast approximate nearest neighbour lookup.

title: Hybrid Search Systems
text: Hybrid search combines lexical retrieval (BM25) and semantic retrieval (dense embeddings) to improve recall and precision over either approach alone.

title: Apache Kafka Architecture
text: Kafka is a distributed event streaming platform. Producers publish messages to topics; consumers read from partitions. It supports high-throughput, fault-tolerant pipelines.

title: Redis Caching Strategies
text: Redis is an in-memory data store used for caching, pub/sub, and session management. TTL-based expiration and LRU eviction keep the cache fresh and bounded.

title: Inverted Index Data Structure
text: An inverted index maps each term to the list of documents containing it. Posting lists store document IDs and term frequencies for fast query evaluation.

title: TF-IDF Weighting
text: TF-IDF weighs a term by how frequently it appears in a document (TF) and how rare it is across all documents (IDF), rewarding discriminative terms.

title: Distributed Systems Fundamentals
text: Distributed systems coordinate multiple nodes to appear as a single coherent system. Key challenges include consistency, availability, partition tolerance, and fault tolerance.

title: Docker and Containerisation
text: Docker packages applications and their dependencies into containers. Docker Compose orchestrates multi-container applications, making local and production environments consistent.

title: REST API Design Principles
text: REST APIs use HTTP verbs and stateless requests. Well-designed APIs follow resource naming conventions, return appropriate status codes, and version endpoints.

title: FastAPI Framework
text: FastAPI is a modern Python web framework for building APIs with automatic OpenAPI documentation, type validation via Pydantic, and async support via Starlette.

title: Evaluation Metrics for Search
text: NDCG measures ranked retrieval quality with graded relevance. MRR captures the rank of the first relevant result. Recall@K measures coverage of relevant documents.

title: Index Sharding for Scalability
text: Sharding distributes an index across multiple nodes or files. Each shard handles a subset of documents, enabling parallel query execution and horizontal scaling.

title: Query Expansion Techniques
text: Query expansion adds related terms to a user query to improve recall. Techniques include pseudo-relevance feedback, synonym expansion, and embedding-based term suggestion.

title: Neural Ranking Models
text: Neural ranking models like ColBERT and MonoT5 use language models to re-rank candidate documents. They outperform BM25 on semantic tasks but are computationally heavier.

title: Knowledge Graphs in Search
text: Knowledge graphs encode entities and relationships. Search engines use them to answer factoid questions directly and to disambiguate query intent.

title: Tokenisation and Text Preprocessing
text: Tokenisation splits text into tokens. Preprocessing steps include lowercasing, stopword removal, stemming, and lemmatisation to normalise vocabulary.

title: Precision and Recall Trade-off
text: Precision measures the fraction of retrieved documents that are relevant. Recall measures the fraction of relevant documents that are retrieved. F1 balances both.

title: Semantic Similarity Benchmarks
text: STS benchmarks evaluate semantic similarity models on sentence pairs. BEIR evaluates retrieval models across diverse domains including biomedical, finance, and news.

title: Attention Mechanism in NLP
text: Attention allows models to focus on relevant parts of the input when generating each output token. Scaled dot-product attention is the core operation in transformers.

title: Word Embeddings: Word2Vec and GloVe
text: Word2Vec learns word embeddings from co-occurrence statistics using skip-gram or CBOW objectives. GloVe uses global matrix factorisation over a word co-occurrence matrix.

title: Large Language Models
text: LLMs trained on massive corpora exhibit emergent capabilities like few-shot learning and chain-of-thought reasoning. Examples include GPT-4, Claude, and Llama.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
text: RAG combines a retrieval system with a generative model. The retriever fetches relevant passages; the generator conditions on them to produce grounded, factual answers.

title: Elasticsearch Architecture
text: Elasticsearch is a distributed search engine built on Apache Lucene. It supports full-text search, aggregations, and near real-time indexing across distributed shards.

title: Latency vs Throughput in Search
text: Latency is the time to return results for a single query. Throughput is the number of queries served per second. Caching, index sharding, and async IO improve both.

title: Data Pipelines with Kafka Streams
text: Kafka Streams is a client library for building stream processing applications. It supports stateful operations like joins and aggregations on top of Kafka topics.

title: Multimodal Search
text: Multimodal search retrieves results across text, images, and video. CLIP embeddings map images and captions to the same vector space, enabling cross-modal queries.

title: Sparse vs Dense Retrieval
text: Sparse retrieval (BM25, TF-IDF) uses term overlap. Dense retrieval uses neural embeddings. SPLADE combines sparsity with learned representations for efficiency and accuracy.

title: Cluster Computing with Spark
text: Apache Spark is a unified analytics engine for large-scale data processing. Its in-memory computation model makes it faster than Hadoop MapReduce for iterative algorithms.

title: Graph Neural Networks
text: Graph neural networks propagate information along edges in a graph. They are applied to citation networks, social graphs, and molecule property prediction.

title: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
text: RLHF fine-tunes language models using human preference data. A reward model is trained on human rankings, then used to optimise the LLM via PPO.

title: Data Serialisation Formats
text: JSON, Avro, and Protobuf are common serialisation formats. Avro and Protobuf are binary and more compact than JSON, making them suitable for high-throughput Kafka pipelines.

title: Microservices Architecture
text: Microservices decompose an application into small independent services. Each service owns its data and communicates via REST or messaging systems like Kafka.

title: Monitoring and Observability
text: Observability relies on metrics, logs, and traces. Prometheus scrapes metrics; Grafana visualises them; Jaeger tracks distributed traces across services.

title: A/B Testing for Search Relevance
text: A/B testing compares two retrieval strategies by routing a fraction of traffic to each. Click-through rate and session success rate measure real-user relevance.

title: Spelling Correction in Search
text: Spelling correction identifies and suggests fixes for misspelled query terms. Noisy channel models and edit-distance algorithms like Levenshtein are commonly used.

title: Faceted Search and Filtering
text: Faceted search lets users narrow results by attributes like category, date, or price. Filters are applied as post-retrieval constraints or pushed into the index query.

title: Learning to Rank
text: Learning to rank trains models to order documents by relevance. Pointwise, pairwise (RankNet), and listwise (LambdaMART) approaches use labeled query-document pairs.

title: Zero-Shot and Few-Shot Learning
text: Zero-shot models generalise to unseen classes without training examples. Few-shot models adapt with only a handful of labelled examples using meta-learning techniques.

title: Named Entity Recognition
text: NER identifies entities such as people, organisations, and locations in text. It is used in search to tag documents and enable entity-based filtering and ranking.

title: Semantic Parsing for Structured Queries
text: Semantic parsing converts natural language queries into structured forms like SQL or SPARQL. It enables question answering over databases and knowledge graphs.

title: Quantisation for Efficient Inference
text: Quantisation reduces model weights from 32-bit floats to 8-bit integers, shrinking memory footprint and speeding up inference with minimal accuracy loss.

title: Future of Search Engines
text: Next-generation search engines will integrate conversational AI, real-time personalisation, multimodal retrieval, and neurosymbolic reasoning to answer complex queries.
